text: Generative AI for game development, templates and frameworks, reusable building blocks for AI stories. Chapter 24, templates and frameworks. The big idea, stop building every narrative system from zero. Create reusable building blocks, templates, and frameworks you can adapt to any genre, mood, or storytelling style. Build once, reuse forever. Three core areas, Python and JSON templates for branching logic and emotion-aware dialogue, Twine structures for modular interactive fiction, and Unity starter kits for narrative-driven 2D or 3D experiences, each with framework code and customization guidance. Template one, the JSON narrative schema. Scenes become nodes, each with text, choices, emotion modifiers, and AI prompt context and dynamic variables. Content separated

From code, swap scenes, localize dialogue, scale to hundreds of nodes without touching the engine. The architecture, JSON nodes feed the Python engine, which renders scenes, tracks emotional state, and branches on player choice. Data tells the story, code runs the machine. Change the JSON, change the game, no recompile. Template two, the Python story engine. Modular, readable, extensible. Load the JSON, render the current scene, update the emotional state, present choices, follow the branch. The engine reads, the data tells. One engine, infinite stories. The case study, a sci-fi mystery. You're a deep space engineer receiving fragmented messages from a vanished crew. Your interpretations shape plot outcomes and emotional tone, and there's always

Fallback text, graceful degradation when the AI is unavailable. Twine, the visual front end. Each passage maps to a story node. Using Harlow or SugarCube with JavaScript, you load the same JSON at runtime, track player state and emotions across passages, and build branching paths that mirror your Python engine visually. The integration, same data, new presentation. The JSON nodes don't change. Twine provides the visual graph where writers link passages intuitively. Macros handle transitions, inventory, and branching. Writers own the flow, developers own the logic. True collaboration. Unity starter kit steps 1 through 4. 1. Load the narrative JSON into game objects. 2. Build the dialogue UI panels, typewriter text, choice buttons.

3. Implement branching logic, choice leads to scene emotion updates. 4. Layer AI-generated responses around the scaffold. Steps 5 and 6. 5. Add audio and visual feedback, voice, portraits, transitions. 6. Build and test, playtest every branch, validate the emotional arcs, then scale 2D or 3D, same data, new presentation. One JSON, many front ends. Templates and frameworks are the hidden scaffolding behind generative storytelling. They let you prototype fast, test cheap, and scale with confidence. Narrative intent plus technical structure, flexible yet purposeful, ready to evolve across platforms. The takeaway, don't start from zero. Build reusable blocks, Python and JSON for logic, Twine for flow, Unity for scale. Spend your energy on emotional

Nuance, not setup code. That's what templates buy you. Your turn, take one scene from your game and write it as a JSON node text, two choices, one emotion modifier. That's your first reusable block. Build the second one tomorrow. That's chapter 24. Next, the final chapter, real-world applications. If this helped, subscribe and I'll see you in video 25.
